title: Actions artifact retention policy
description: One row per artifact name family: how many days its uploads keep the artifact, who reads it, and why that length is needed. scripts/check-artifact-retention.sh holds every actions/upload-artifact step to its row and states the matching rule.

propertyNames.description: An exact artifact name, or a literal prefix followed by `*`.

retention-days.description: Days an upload keeps the artifact: 1 to 89, or `max` for the repository maximum of 90, which needs a max-reader.

readers.description: Each reader: a repository path, then what reads it and how far back.

max-reader.description: With retention-days `max`: the path of the reader that needs 90 days, one of the readers.

scan.description: Whether the family is a lane or eval artifact that a leak scan (lib/publish-gate.mjs scanLeak) clears before it leaves the run. `upload`: each upload step follows a .github/actions/scan-upload step over the same path, whose clean output its `if:` requires, or reads from the read runner's leak-scan output directory. `plaintext`: the upload is sealed ciphertext, so a scan step over the plaintext comes earlier in the same steps. `none`: not a lane or eval artifact; the reason says why.

computed-by.description: The script whose step output sets each upload's retention-days as `${{ steps.<id>.outputs.retention-days }}`; retention-days records the longest it returns.

pending-cut.description: A shorter retention found safe or under owner review and not yet made; the row still records today's value.

uploads.description: For an upload whose name starts with an expression: `<workflow or action path>#<job id>` of each job uploading this family.
